claims.text: The rider's own claim measures the excess against the solo-rider optimal (11.5 km), but this is a RYDE_POOL trip. Under POL-RD-12 the baseline for POL-RD-01 is the matched-itinerary optimal recorded in trip_record.optimal_distance_km, which is 16.0 km, not the solo figure of 11.5 km. The rider has cited the wrong field and the claim fails on that ground alone.

The governing distance is the GPS trace figure of 16.96 km, not the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km of 17.0 km, because POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing field. Against the matched-itinerary optimal of 16.0 km the excess is 0.96 km, which is 6.00% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests must pass: the excess must exceed 20% of optimal AND exceed 0.8 km. The percentage test fails decisively at 6.00%, so no deviation is established.

The derived deviation block on the trace itself records status 'no deviation', with excess_km 0.96 and excess_pct 6.00 against the 16.0 km optimal. The trace is COMPLETE, 100.0% coverage, 133 fixes at a 10 s interval with zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0 s, so there is no POL-RD-07 impairment and no basis to look for independent corroboration. The measurement is clean and it is below threshold.

The driver's explanation is that the co-rider pickup is part of the pooled itinerary, and the trip record corroborates it: vehicle_type is RYDE_POOL and optimal_route_source records a 'matched pooled itinerary with one co-rider'. Distance attributable to collecting a co-rider on a platform-matched pooled itinerary is never a deviation under POL-RD-12 and is excluded from excess before POL-RD-01 is applied. The 0.96 km residual is exactly that kind of itinerary distance.

The rider's arithmetic is also wrong on its own terms. The rider says the app matched 16.0 km but 'we drove 16.96 km' and then complains of a $23.51 fare. The fare breakdown shows the distance charge was computed on 17.0 km at $0.75/km = $12.75, plus $6.16 time charge, $3.80 base and $0.80 platform fee, totalling $23.51. The rider was billed for the pooled itinerary, not for a solo route, and the fare reconciles to the ledger with zero ERP lines.

No exculpatory clause is needed because no deviation is established, but the record is also free of any billing-integrity defect: erp_gantries is empty, tolls_erp is 0.0, airport_surcharge is 0.0, and the fare ledger reconciles to total_charged of $23.51. There is no phantom gantry and no wrongly applied surcharge to refund under POL-RD-09(4).

The rider's profile does not assist the claim. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the POL-RD-08 corroboration uplift for a serial claimant (4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated) is not engaged. The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and has not discharged it: the excess measured from the unimpaired trace does not meet the POL-RD-01 threshold.

The driver's profile is clean for the POL-RD-06 test: deviation_flags_90d is 1, well below the 3-flag threshold, and 1/173 completed_trips_90d is 0.006, far below the 0.05 ratio. No repeat-deviation pattern is established, and no conduct referral is warranted. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is context only under POL-GEN-01 and is not the trailing-90-day figure POL-RD-06 asks for.

The traffic advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-02836-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so no advisory covers the Blk 231 Serangoon Ave 3 corridor in this window. Neither party has cited it as an exculpatory ground, so POL-RD-13(1) applies: the absence is a gap in the bundle, not a contradiction, and it does not trigger POL-RD-10(5). It is cited here only to record that no external traffic cause is on file and none is needed, because the deviation fails at the threshold.

The chat log is empty: message_count 0, no messages, not truncated. There is therefore no rider instruction in the chat log that could exonerate any distance under POL-RD-04, and equally no rider instruction that the trace failed to corroborate under POL-RD-14. The record is silent on both sides, and the case is decided on the trace and the matched-itinerary baseline alone.

The rider's claim that the driver 'picked up someone else' is not a deviation at all on this product. The trip record shows vehicle_type RYDE_POOL and the routing engine matched a pooled itinerary with one co-rider at booking time.
